---
title: "An anonymous function in the native pipe needs parentheses and a call"
ref: PIP-03
categories: [Pipes]
impact: incoherent
attendu: "`\"bbc\" \"bbb\"`"
versions: "Since R 4.1.0 (native pipe and `\\(x)` syntax)"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
#| eval: false
words <- c("abc", "bab")
words |> \(y) gsub("a", replacement = "b", x = y)
words |> (\(y) gsub("a", replacement = "b", x = y))
```
:::

Run this block: the first form gives "function 'function' not supported in RHS call of a pipe", the second "function '(' not supported in RHS call of a pipe".

## Why

On the right of `|>`, R expects a function call, into which it inserts the value as the first argument. A function definition `\(y) ...` is not a call, and neither is a definition in parentheses: R rejects both as soon as it parses the code.

With `%>%`, `x %>% (\(y) ...)` works, without the call parentheses. The native pipe requires you to call the function explicitly, with a trailing `()` that looks superfluous.

## The remedy

Wrap the function in parentheses and call it. Since R 4.2.0, the `_` placeholder often removes the need for an anonymous function.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
words <- c("abc", "bab")
words |> (\(y) gsub("a", replacement = "b", x = y))()
words |> gsub(pattern = "a", replacement = "b", x = _)
```
:::
